Summary: The paper builds a controlled harness for writing OMIM-style phenotype entries from exactly the papers curators cited (100 entries with 2-12 references; 515 papers, 19% readable in full via open access), with one model (Claude Opus 5.5) doing all writing, extraction, auditing and judging. Four reading strategies (direct long-context reading, an agentic curator, an evidence graph, a case table), a memory-first strategy, a memory-only control and several add-ons are compared on a primary recall endpoint: coverage of 6,652 atomic facts split once from OMIM's allelic-variant descriptions as deposited in ClinVar. Main results: (i) hiding the full text of the same papers lowers coverage of their facts from 79.8% to 36.1% (+43.7 points, 95% CI 38.3-49.1, 46 entries; Fig. 2a, Table 24); (ii) at the main settings no strategy beats direct reading on the 93 entries all completed (agent -0.6, graph -0.5, case table -1.9; Table 1), with the order depending on entry subset and extraction settings (Table 21, Appendix E); (iii) on 38 held-out entries a per-paper completeness pass adds 2.6 points while lengthening drafts by a third (Tables 30, 34), and the gain on all 41 depends on keeping the unrevised draft when the safety filter stops the revision (Table 32); (iv) a planted-error test shows the claim-level audit catches citation swaps and single-value substitutions but not added citations (best-verdict rule) or omissions (Fig. 4, Tables 50-53). The paper labels every analysis as pre-specified, post hoc or exploratory and releases drafts, verdicts and scores but not the curator-derived fact lists.
Strengths: Strong experimental hygiene for an LLM-pipeline comparison: one model, the same guards, audit and scoring for every strategy, paired comparisons over entries with bootstrap intervals and sign tests, and a symmetric completion rule that compares strategies only on entries all completed, with an intention-to-treat sensitivity (Section 3.3, Tables 5, 7, 8, 11).

Unusually transparent reporting of analysis status. Section 3.3 and Appendix Table 2 list every post hoc choice (a)-(i), including the switch to fixed fact lists and the symmetric rule that turned a -2.1 point evidence-graph deficit into a non-significant -0.5 (Appendix M.4). Deviations from planned sizes are documented (Appendices J, K, L).

The hidden-full-text experiment manipulates access within the same papers and entries rather than comparing across papers, which removes the confounding by creation era and journal that affects the observational by-access tables (Section 4.1, Table 24 vs. Table 13). The effect is large and consistent (45 of 46 entries better, 1 tied).

Run-to-run and judge variation are measured and used correctly as yardsticks rather than tests (Appendix E, Table 20). The 30-entry replicate set also shows that the evidence graph's sign flips with the entries averaged, not with replicate noise, which is a useful caution for the field.

The memory-only control stratified by creation era, including 20 compared entries created in 2026 and held out from all development, is a sensible empirical contamination check (Section 4.2, Fig. 5, Table 16, Appendix M.2). Causal-gene F1 from the header alone falls from 88.9-100% in older bands to 41.2% and 30.0% in the newest, which supports interpreting reading-strategy coverage as more than recall.

The audit stress test is informative about a concrete design flaw: under the best-verdict-over-cited-papers rule, 0 of 30 added irrelevant citations were flagged although the added paper's own verdict was 'unsupported' for all 176 attributed claims (Section 4.5, Table 50, Appendix L). The stored-audit replay showing 4-7% of (claim, cited paper) pairs unsupported in real multi-citation paragraphs (Table 53) turns this into an actionable finding.

Costs, calls, tokens and safety-filter stops are reported per strategy and experiment (Tables 12, 34, 42, 48, 49), and the released pipelines' settings changes are documented in detail (Tables 37-39).
Weaknesses: No human validation of any judgement, and the writer, extractor, auditor and both judges ('conveyed' and 'stated') are the same model family. The only reliability evidence is 95.7% self-agreement between two judgings (Appendix E). The strategy differences that carry the main comparison are 0.5-1.9 points (Table 1) and the reading-better gains 1.6-3.3 points (Table 30), exactly the size most exposed to systematic judge error or self-preference. The paper concedes this (Limitation i) but a benchmark paper without even a small stratified expert check of the fact judge leaves the levels and small differences unvalidated.

The main comparison is not matched on settings: writers run at high effort, but per-paper extraction in the evidence graph and case table runs at medium effort with synopsis terms (and the table's inheritance) assigned by rule (Section 3.2). The headline 'no design beat direct reading' is therefore partly a statement about a handicapped configuration. The matched ablation that addresses this is post hoc, on 38 entries chosen with more full text, and changes two factors at once (Section 4.2, Appendix F, Tables 21-23); on it the matched evidence graph is +1.8 (+0.4 to +3.3) above direct reading.

The regime tested makes the null result on strategies close to expected. Inputs are small (the padding appendix gives a median of 39,450 characters across 2-8 papers, Table 44), 81% of papers are abstract or title only, and 2,669 of 6,239 compared facts are not stated in the supplied text at all (Table 19). Long-context reading of a few abstracts in one prompt leaves little room for agents or intermediate representations. The regime where designs might separate (many relevant papers) could not be compared because of safety-filter stops (Section 4.4, Appendix K.2, M.1). The generality of the comparative finding is therefore narrow, as the paper itself says (Section 5).

The access effect is close to definitional for this reference. The reference is OMIM's variant-centred allelic-variant prose, written by curators who read full papers, so a writer given only the abstract cannot convey most of its facts. Figure 2b shows the supplied text states 76% of facts about full-text papers but 26% of those about abstract-only papers. Measuring the size (+43.7 points) is useful, but the qualitative conclusion that 'access bounds agreement' adds little beyond prior full-text vs. abstract text-mining results (Westergaard et al., 2018), which the paper cites.

Construct validity of the primary endpoint is limited. Strategies write whole phenotype entries but are scored only on per-paper variant facts taken from OMIM gene entries. About 24% of a direct-reading draft's statements have a counterpart in the reference (Appendix H, Limitation v). The endpoint is recall-only, with no precision or length counterpart (Section 3.3). The completeness pass's +2.6 points comes with 14,412 vs 10,802 characters and 164 vs 129 claims per audited entry (Section 4.3, Table 34), and no length-matched baseline is run. The only precision-side check is the audit's supported share on 20 entries with no interval (Table 33).

The benchmark is not reusable as released. The fixed fact lists contain curator wording and are not redistributed, so anyone scoring a new strategy must rebuild the reference under the rights holder's terms and re-split it. The stability of a fresh split by the same procedure was not measured, while a different splitting procedure shifted levels by 2-5 points (Section 3.1 'Reuse', Table 6). Given strategy differences of 0.5-1.9 points, results on a rebuilt reference cannot be compared with those reported here, which weakens contribution (1) as a benchmark.

Completion is itself an outcome of the strategy and is shaped by an opaque safety filter. 7 of 100 main entries drop out (Table 5), 10 of 30 entries created in 2026 (Appendix M.2), every new large entry (Appendix K.2), and all of STORM (Appendix J). Comparisons on completed entries condition on a post-treatment variable. The ITT analysis moves the agent's difference from -0.6 to +0.4 and widens the case table's interval to include zero (Table 11). The reading-better gain flips sign under the zero-imputation rule (-3.5 and -4.8; Table 32).

Several analyses that shape the narrative are post hoc or very small: the restrictions by what the text states (which give the case table's -8.4 point gap on 40 entries), the matched ablation, the fourth reading-better arm, the padding results on 2 or 6 entries and the released-pipeline runs on 10 and 4 entries (Appendix Tables 2-3). The labelling is honest, but the result is many small, conditional findings rather than one well-powered pre-registered contrast. The subset-dependence claim for the evidence graph (+3.1 on the ablation's 'other 19' entries) includes the single all-full-text entry, on which the graph is +17.8 (Table 14) and which alone contributes about 0.9 points to that mean.

Each paradigm has one implementation, and the agentic curator's tool use is self-reported rather than logged (Appendix B). Released systems ran in non-default configurations (PaperQA2 without its agent, six concatenated question answers, a 384-dimension shared embedder; Tables 37-38), so they say little about those designs, as the paper acknowledges.

Clarity suffers from extreme density. The abstract and Sections 4.2-4.4 pack many numbers, intervals and caveats into single sentences (e.g. the abstract's 'on all 41, it requires keeping the unrevised draft where the model's safety filter stopped the revision', and Section 4.4 compressing four experiments into one paragraph). Key definitions such as 'stated', 'repaired' and 'like for like' must be held in mind across a 55-page document, much of the evidence lives in the appendix, and the main text is hard to follow without it.
Questions: Can you add even a small expert validation, for example 200-300 (fact, draft) 'conveyed' judgements and 'stated' judgements stratified by access level and strategy, with chance-corrected agreement? Without it, how confident are you that the 0.5-1.9 point differences in Table 1 and the 2.6 point completeness gain are not judge artefacts?
Could a second model family serve as the fact judge on a subset (e.g. the 30 replicate entries) to test self-preference and correlated errors between the 'stated' and 'conveyed' judgements?

Can you report a length-controlled view of the reading-better arms, for example a direct-reading baseline instructed to write about 14,000 characters, or coverage per 1,000 characters, so that the completeness pass's gain can be separated from writing more?

Why was the pre-specified main comparison run with medium-effort extraction and rule-assigned synopsis terms for the extract-then-write strategies while writers ran at high effort? Would you consider the matched setting the fair comparison, and if so, what does the 93-entry comparison look like under it?

How stable are levels and differences under a fresh split of the same paragraphs by the same procedure? Re-splitting a subset (e.g. 30 entries) would tell readers who rebuild the reference how comparable their numbers are to yours.
Is there a way to release the reference in a form usable without redistributing curator wording, such as a hosted scoring service over fact identifiers, so that the benchmark can be reused?

Do safety-filter stops cluster by disease area, paper content or strategy step (e.g. per-paper extraction vs. single-prompt writing)? If they do, how might conditioning on completion bias the comparisons?

Of the variants the extract-then-write strategies write that OMIM does not list (111 for the graph and 130 for the case table against 36 for direct reading; Table 10), how many are actually reported in the cited papers? Precision counts them as misses whether or not the paper reports them.
How sensitive is the evidence graph's +3.1 on the ablation's 'other 19' entries to the single all-full-text entry (+17.8 in Table 14)?

For the 'not stated' facts that reading strategies still convey at 5.5-6.9%, can you separate inference (e.g. inheritance mode from zygosity) from recall, for example by checking against the memory-only control per fact rather than per entry?
Limitations: All judgements (writing, extraction, auditing, fact conveyance, 'stated' availability) come from one model family, with no human or cross-family validation.
The fixed fact lists are not redistributed, and fresh-split stability is unmeasured, so external reuse with comparable numbers is not possible.

The regime is narrow: 2-12 references, mostly abstracts, small inputs, well-annotated molecularly characterised entries. Large relevant-paper sets could not be compared because of safety-filter stops.
The primary endpoint is recall-only on a variant-centred reference that covers about a quarter of draft content. There is no precision or length control on the primary endpoint.
Opaque safety-filter stops remove entries unevenly across strategies, and every comparison on completed entries conditions on an outcome of the strategy.
Main settings are unmatched across paradigms. The matched ablation is post hoc, on 38 entries, and changes two factors at once.
The main strategies were developed on their evaluation entries. Held-out evidence is limited to 20 compared 2026 entries and the 41-entry reading-better split.
There is one implementation per paradigm, the agent's tool use is not logged, and the released systems ran in non-default configurations.
